newsitem.title: THAILAND: Amnuay sees easier dollar benefiting Thai baht.
newsitem.headline: Amnuay sees easier dollar benefiting Thai baht.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Monday that Thailand's economy and its baht would benefit from a weaker U.S. dollar.

Amnuay told reporters he backed a weekend resolution of the G7 industrial countries that said the U.S. dollar could not continue rallying much higher and that wild fluctuations in foreign exchange rates were undesirable.
He said the Thai baht had adjusted well against the recent surge of the dollar because of the way it was fixed against a basket of major currencies, dominated by the dollar.
The baht steadied after the message was delivered by the G7 meeting and the currency on Monday was bid/offered at 25.935-25.945 at 0836 GMT against quotes of 25.990-26.040 late on Friday.
Amnuay said the baht had now depreciated to about 25.90 to the dollar now from 25.05 in late 1995.
The baht came under severe pressure from offshore speculators in past weeks as the central bank continued to fix the currency at new lows each time the dollar rallied in overseas markets.
The sagging baht has forced the central bank to intervene in the foreign exchange markets on occasions to keep the currency from plummeting on speculator selling pressures.
The Bank of Thailand has also maintained a high interest rate regime to keep support the currency. The overnight interbank rate was quoted on Monday at 24-25 percent.
The minister said he expected to see a more stable dollar over the next one to two years.
